account:
Today seems quiet from what I have personally heard. I made my market walk, checked the treasury during town accounts, and found 128 emeralds. The secretary said no bills, council papers, or further correspondence had reached them earlier today. I have just returned from tea and asked whether anything arrived in my absence; I have not yet heard an answer.

The neighbour described the riverside as peaceful, with no trouble personally observed and no request for town hall. They also passed along the baker's announcement that fresh bread would be at the market stall today. That sounds like ordinary trade and neighbours spreading useful news, not evidence of anything unusual.

The most notable new business is the innkeeper's request to discuss the inn's service to town tomorrow at eighteen in the great hall. We agreed to meet at my office at seventeen forty-five and walk there together, and I asked the secretary to record it. I do not yet know the proposal's details or why the innkeeper wants the discussion, so I should not assume more. Tomorrow also includes a morning grain inspection at the mill and the usual afternoon tea.

Earlier I heard residents asking the builder for an update on town works, but I did not hear a substantive report. On returning to town hall I saw the builder walking with a lantern; I do not know its purpose. Nothing I have seen establishes a particular problem or unusual scheme. My immediate business is to hear the secretary's afternoon update and remain available at the office before going home at nineteen.
